dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: There are students from so many countries in our class!
dialogue.reading: ðɛr ər ˈstuːdənts frəm soʊ ˈmɛni ˈkʌntriz ɪn aʊr ˈklæs!

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: I know! Yesterday I met students from the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia.
dialogue.reading: aɪ ˈnoʊ! ˈjɛstərdeɪ aɪ ˈmɛt ˈstuːdənts frəm ðə juˈnaɪtɪd ˈsteɪts, ðə juˈnaɪtɪd ˈkɪŋdəm ənd ɔːˈstreɪljə.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Have you been to any other English-speaking countries?
dialogue.reading: hæv juː bɪn tu ˈɛni ˈʌðər ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˌspiːkɪŋ ˈkʌntriz?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: No, Canada is my first. Have you been to the UK?
dialogue.reading: ˈnoʊ, ˈkænədə ɪz maɪ ˈfɜːrst. hæv juː bɪn tə ðə ˌjuːˈkeɪ?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Yes, I studied in London for a year. And my sister lives in New Zealand.
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs, aɪ ˈstʌdid ɪn ˈlʌndən fər ə ˈjɪr. ənd maɪ ˈsɪstər ˈlɪvz ɪn ˈnuː ˈziːlənd.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Lucky you! Is New Zealand like Australia?
dialogue.reading: ˈlʌki juː! ɪz ˈnuː ˈziːlənd ˈlaɪk ɔːˈstreɪljə?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Not really. It's much smaller, and it's cooler.
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːt ˈriːli. ɪts ˈmʌtʃ ˈsmɔːlər, ənd ɪts ˈkuːlər.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Can I ask a grammar question? Why do we say "the United States" but just "Canada"?
dialogue.reading: kən aɪ ˈæsk ə ˈɡræmər ˈkwɛstʃən? ˈwaɪ duː wiː ˈseɪ ðə juˈnaɪtɪd ˈsteɪts bʌt dʒʌst ˈkænədə?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Good question! We use "the" when the name has a word like "States" or "Kingdom."
dialogue.reading: ˈɡʊd ˈkwɛstʃən! wiː ˈjuːz ðə wɛn ðə ˈneɪm ˈhæz ə ˈwɜːrd ˈlaɪk ˈsteɪts ɔːr ˈkɪŋdəm.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: So "the US" and "the UK," but "Thailand" and "Japan."
dialogue.reading: soʊ ðə ˌjuːˈɛs ənd ðə ˌjuːˈkeɪ, bʌt ˈtaɪlænd ənd dʒəˈpæn.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Exactly. And "the Philippines," because it's a group of islands.
dialogue.reading: ɪɡˈzæktli. ənd ðə ˈfɪlɪpiːnz, bɪˈkɔːz ɪts ə ˈɡruːp əv ˈaɪləndz.
